samasa.type: karmadhāraya (avadhāraṇa-pūrvapada: the first member identifies the form)
samasa.literal: by the form that is faith
samasa.sense: as faith, in the shape of faith
samasa.alt: Also read as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, श्रद्धायाः रूपम् ‘the form of faith’. The karmadhāraya fits better: the Goddess is not said to own a form belonging to faith but to be present as faith itself.

morph.note: श्रद्धा is formed from श्रत् ‘trust, truth’ (treated like a verbal prefix) + √धा ‘to place’ (juhotyādi, 3) with the feminine suffix -ā: ‘placing (one’s heart) in what is true’. The t of श्रत् becomes d before dh (श्रद्धा).
Past passive participle of सम् + √स्था, as in 5.35-37: ‘(who) abides’, with अस्ति understood.

mantras.anvaya: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु श्रद्धारूपेण संस्थिता (अस्ति), तस्यै नमः (अस्तु), तस्यै नमः, तस्यै नमः, नमः नमः।
mantras.anvaya_en: The relative clause (या … संस्थिता) and its correlative (तस्यै), as in 5.35-37.
mantras.lit: The Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of faith — homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.
mantras.tr: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as faith: salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her — salutation again and again.
mantras.tr_note: ‘As’ renders the instrumental -रूपेण ‘in the form of’; ‘again and again’ renders the doubled नमो नमः.

comm.t: The Goddess is named as faith (श्रद्धा): the trust that sets the heart on what it holds true.

The gods said in chapter 4 that she is ‘faith in the good’ (4.5: श्रद्धा सतां). In the wider Hindu tradition faith shapes the person: the Bhagavad Gītā (17.3) says ‘a person is made of faith; as one’s faith is, so is one’ (श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः).
A modern reflection: on this reading faith is not only something a person has; it is a presence of the Goddess in the person. Trust itself becomes a place of meeting.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (avadhāraṇa-pūrvapada: the first member identifies the form)
samasa.literal: by the form that is loveliness
samasa.sense: as loveliness, in the shape of loveliness
samasa.alt: Also read as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, कान्तेः रूपम् ‘the form of loveliness’. The karmadhāraya fits better: the Goddess is not said to own a form belonging to loveliness but to be present as loveliness itself.

morph.note: कान्ति is an action noun with -ति (क्तिन्), usually derived from √कम् ‘to desire, love’ (bhvādi, 1Ā): ‘what is desired’, hence loveliness, charm; the vowel lengthens as in शान्ति. A derivation from √कन् ‘to shine’ is also given, which brings out the sense ‘radiance’.
Past passive participle of सम् + √स्था, as in 5.35-37: ‘(who) abides’, with अस्ति understood.

mantras.anvaya: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु कान्तिरूपेण संस्थिता (अस्ति), तस्यै नमः (अस्तु), तस्यै नमः, तस्यै नमः, नमः नमः।
mantras.anvaya_en: The relative clause (या … संस्थिता) and its correlative (तस्यै), as in 5.35-37.
mantras.lit: The Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of loveliness — homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.
mantras.tr: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as loveliness: salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her — salutation again and again.
mantras.tr_note: ‘As’ renders the instrumental -रूपेण ‘in the form of’; ‘again and again’ renders the doubled नमो नमः.

comm.t: The Goddess is named as loveliness, the radiance (कान्ति) by which anything is beautiful.

Beauty is here a presence of the Goddess, not a lure away from her. The next part of the story turns on exactly this: Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa see her beauty (5.89–92) and tell Śumbha, who wants to possess what he can only worship.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has कान्तिः as name 449, in the same run as शान्तिः (447).

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (avadhāraṇa-pūrvapada: the first member identifies the form)
samasa.literal: by the form that is fortune
samasa.sense: as Lakṣmī, as fortune and prosperity
samasa.alt: Also read as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, लक्ष्म्याः रूपम् ‘the form of Lakṣmī’ — the goddess Lakṣmī as one form of the Devī. The karmadhāraya keeps the pattern of the hymn (‘in the form that is fortune’); both readings agree that Lakṣmī is the Devī herself.

morph.note: लक्ष्मी is traditionally derived (uṇādi) from √लक्ष् ‘to mark’: the auspicious mark, good fortune. It is one of the few feminine ī-stems that keep the nominative -s (लक्ष्मीः, not *लक्ष्मी); inside the compound the bare stem stands.
Past passive participle of सम् + √स्था, as in 5.35-37: ‘(who) abides’, with अस्ति understood.

mantras.anvaya: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु लक्ष्मीरूपेण संस्थिता (अस्ति), तस्यै नमः (अस्तु), तस्यै नमः, तस्यै नमः, नमः नमः।
mantras.anvaya_en: The relative clause (या … संस्थिता) and its correlative (तस्यै), as in 5.35-37.
mantras.lit: The Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of fortune — homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.
mantras.tr: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as fortune: salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her — salutation again and again.
mantras.tr_note: ‘As’ renders the instrumental -रूपेण ‘in the form of’; ‘again and again’ renders the doubled नमो नमः.

comm.t: The Goddess is named as Lakṣmī, fortune and prosperity, present in all beings. Prosperity is not a separate goddess’s gift here but one of her own forms.

In chapter 4 the gods said she is ‘Śrī herself in the homes of the virtuous, and misfortune (अलक्ष्मी) in those of the wicked’ (4.5). In the Gita Press pāṭha the middle carita is assigned to Mahālakṣmī; that assignment is liturgical tradition, not a statement of this verse.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has महालक्ष्मीः as name 210. The two texts remain separate works.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (avadhāraṇa-pūrvapada: the first member identifies the form)
samasa.literal: by the form that is activity
samasa.sense: as activity, in the shape of activity
samasa.alt: Also read as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, वृत्तेः रूपम् ‘the form of activity’. The karmadhāraya fits better: the Goddess is not said to own a form belonging to activity but to be present as activity itself.

morph.note: वृत्ति is an action noun from √वृत् ‘to turn, to be, to go on’ (bhvādi, 1Ā, वर्तते) with -ति (क्तिन्): a turning, a mode of being; hence conduct, occupation, livelihood — and, in the language of Yoga, a movement of the mind.
Past passive participle of सम् + √स्था, as in 5.35-37: ‘(who) abides’, with अस्ति understood.

mantras.anvaya: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु वृत्तिरूपेण संस्थिता (अस्ति), तस्यै नमः (अस्तु), तस्यै नमः, तस्यै नमः, नमः नमः।
mantras.anvaya_en: The relative clause (या … संस्थिता) and its correlative (तस्यै), as in 5.35-37.
mantras.lit: The Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of activity — homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.
mantras.tr: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as the activity by which each lives: salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her — salutation again and again.
mantras.tr_note: ‘As’ renders the instrumental -रूपेण ‘in the form of’; ‘again and again’ renders the doubled नमो नमः.

comm.t: The Goddess is named as वृत्ति: the activity by which every being goes on living — its way of life, its means of sustenance.

Two senses are current. The common one is livelihood: what supports each creature’s life. Another takes वृत्ति as the movements of the mind (the Yoga term चित्तवृत्ति), so that every mental state is her form. The hymn’s neighbours (memory, faith, delusion) allow the second; the plain sense of ‘all beings’ favours the first.
A modern reflection: on either reading, ordinary work and ordinary thought are not outside the sacred. The means by which one lives is named as a form of the Goddess.

flags.uncertain: वृत्ति may be ‘livelihood, way of life’ or ‘a movement of the mind’; the edition prefers the first and notes the second.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (avadhāraṇa-pūrvapada: the first member identifies the form)
samasa.literal: by the form that is memory
samasa.sense: as memory, in the shape of memory
samasa.alt: Also read as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, स्मृतेः रूपम् ‘the form of memory’. The karmadhāraya fits better: the Goddess is not said to own a form belonging to memory but to be present as memory itself.

morph.note: स्मृति is an action noun from √स्मृ ‘to remember’ (bhvādi, 1P, स्मरति) with -ति (क्तिन्): memory, remembrance; also, as a term, the remembered tradition (the Smṛti texts).
Past passive participle of सम् + √स्था, as in 5.35-37: ‘(who) abides’, with अस्ति understood.

mantras.anvaya: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु स्मृतिरूपेण संस्थिता (अस्ति), तस्यै नमः (अस्तु), तस्यै नमः, तस्यै नमः, नमः नमः।

mantras.lit: The Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of memory — homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.
mantras.tr: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as memory: salutation to her, salutation to her, salutation to her — salutation again and again.
mantras.tr_note: ‘As’ renders the instrumental -रूपेण ‘in the form of’; ‘again and again’ renders the doubled नमो नमः.

comm.t: The Goddess is named as memory (स्मृति) in every creature.

Remembering her is the act this whole episode turns on: she had promised to destroy the gods’ calamities whenever they remembered her (5.6), and the gods’ hymn in chapter 4 says ‘remembered, you take away fear’ (4.17: दुर्गे स्मृता हरसि भीतिम्). Brahmā’s hymn calls her महास्मृतिः, the great memory (1.77). Here the power of remembering is itself her form.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has स्मृतिः as name 540.
A modern reflection: the faculty by which one turns to the divine is already the divine at work. Memory is not only a store of the past but a way back.
